To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

acquired angio‐ oedema (AAO) is associated with autoantibody formation and that autoantibodies against C1‐INhibitor (C1‐ INH) are present in the majority of cases of AAO, and that these autoantibodies may be either paraproteins or IgG molecules.
(1) the majority of patients with acquired angio‐edema have autoantibody to C1 inhibitor; (2) the autoantibodies cleave C1 inhibitor; and (3) the paraproteins in some cases are autoantibody.
the large majority of patients with acquired angio‐ oedema (AAO) have anti‐C1‐inhibitor autoantibodies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of autoantibodies against C1‐IN inhibitor (C1INH) in acquired angioedema (AA) in 13 patients, 12 of whom had C1INH autoantobodies and 12 cleaved C1INH.
the study of the mechanisms of acquired C1‐inhibitor deficiency and the pathogenesis of angio‐ oedema.
the study of the pathogenetic mechanisms of the disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AAE is a disease of autoantibodies.
autoantibodies against C1‐IN‐H are the cause of the acquired deficiency of this serine protease inhibitor.
AAE is an autoimmune disease, which is frequently associated with lymphoproliferation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of autoantibodies is necessary and sufficient for the generation of AAE.
autoantibodies and paraproteins are the major cause of acquired C1‐ INH deficiency.
autoantibodies against C1‐INAH are the main cause of acquired deficiency of C1‐inhibitor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
acquired angio‐edema (AAED) is a heterogeneous disease with multiple causes, including autoantibodies against C1‐esterase inhibitor (C1INH), which can also be found in patients without AAE.
acquired C1 inhibitor deficiency (acquired angi-oedema) is a disease that is associated with a variety of lymphoproliterative diseases.

the presence of autoantibodies and the cleaved form in the plasma of patients with AAE is a strong indication for a thorough investigation for lymphoproliferation, which may be the cause of the autoantibodies.
